# Mateu

> Mateu defines business UIs agnostically. One model, authored three ways that produce the same thing: YAML files (`type: UI` mounts, `routes.yaml`, page definitions, `sources.yaml`), the WYSIWYG visual editor in IntelliJ/VS Code (which writes that YAML), or code in Java (`@UI`), C# (`[UI]`) or Python (`@ui`). Rendered anywhere: web (Vaadin; Oracle Redwood, also embedded in Visual Builder apps), mobile (the generic Mateu app on iOS/Android), desktop (IntelliJ). Served by any backend or by none: Java on Spring Boot MVC/WebFlux, Quarkus, Micronaut or Helidon MP, ASP.NET Core, FastAPI — or a static bundle on a CDN. UIs from different domains federate into one console. The backend is an option, not the definition.

All authoring paths and servers emit one versioned wire model (JSON); every renderer consumes it. Generated JSON Schemas give editors validation and completion for every YAML file.

## AI reference files

- [Build UIs with AI](https://mateu.io/build-uis-with-ai/): the Claude Code plugin, AGENTS.md in every project, these files, the JSON Schemas and MCP
- [Full documentation as text](https://mateu.io/llms-full.txt): every page of this site in one file, generated at build time
- [Compact reference](https://mateu.io/mateu-ai-compact.md): ~2 500 tokens — key annotations, patterns, return types. Use for day-to-day code generation.
- [Full reference](https://mateu.io/mateu-ai-full.md): ~9 000 tokens — complete annotation catalogue, all interfaces, all UX patterns.
- Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add miguelperezcolom/mateu` then `/plugin install mateu@mateu` — skills `mateu` (Java), `mateu-screen`, `mateu-yaml` (YAML + static bundles), `mateu-dotnet`, `mateu-python`, `mateu-scaffold`, `mateu-run`, `mateu-federation` ([source](https://github.com/miguelperezcolom/mateu/tree/master/ai/claude-plugin/mateu/skills))
- JSON Schemas for every `specs/ui` YAML file: [specs-schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/mateu/master/backend/shared/uidl/specs-schema.json) (all file kinds), [uidl-schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/mateu/master/backend/shared/uidl/uidl-schema.json) (components)
- [Agent operability (MCP)](https://mateu.io/reference/agent-operability/): operate a running app's screens as MCP tools · [Prompt-to-app](https://mateu.io/reference/prompt-to-app/): an LLM writes the UI as data, checked against the schemas
- [Use Mateu with AI assistants](https://mateu.io/ai-assistant-reference/): loading the references in Claude Projects, Gemini, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot

## Key concepts (YAML path)

- Everything lives under `specs/ui/` (on the classpath for a Java backend, e.g. `src/main/resources/specs/ui`). Start each file with `$schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/mateu/master/backend/shared/uidl/specs-schema.json` and validate against it.
- A `type: UI` file is a mount (the YAML twin of `@UI`): its base path, its route files and its `home:` route.
- `routes.yaml` (`type: Routes`) binds each mount-relative route to a `layout:` (a definition file) and/or a `viewModel:` (a class), with `fixedParams`/`defaultParams`; one definition can serve several routes.
- A definition file is a page: a component tree (`type: Listing`, `Form`, layouts, cards…), optionally with `actions:` beside `layout:` to write through a `restAction`.
- `sources.yaml` names each REST endpoint once (`itemsPath`, `totalPath`, `fields`, `proxy`, `sample:` data); pages reference it by `ref:`. Secrets only as `${secret.KEY}` on proxied sources.
- `type: AppShell` is the chrome and the menu. Other kinds: actions, types, translations, environments, `project.yaml`, partials.
- An unparseable definition answers "Not found" (the reason is in the server log, or on the page with `-Dmateu.dev=true`); unknown keys are ignored silently.
- No backend: the `mateu-bundle-maven-plugin` bundles `specs/ui` into static files for any CDN (`specsOnly`, `staticOnly` fails the build on anything that needs a server).

## Key concepts (Java path)

- `@UI("/path")` on a class registers it as a routed view; no path means root. It is the only routing annotation: inner routes go in `routes.yaml`.
- A routed view model is instantiated fresh on every request (not a singleton bean).
- Actions are declared: only `@Action`/`@Button`/`@Toolbar`… methods (or ids the view itself advertises) run — strict mode is the default.
- Fields → form fields. `List<T>` fields → grids/tables. Nested class fields → subforms.
- Methods annotated with `@Button` or `@Toolbar` become buttons.
- Bean validation (`@NotNull`, `@NotEmpty`, `@Min`, `@Max`) is enforced client-side and server-side automatically.
- `HttpRequest` can be added to any method signature; Mateu injects it.
- Action methods return: `void` (stay), `URI` (navigate), `Message` (toast), any Java object (open as view), `PageBanner` (show banner), `new State(this)` (update without navigating).
- CRUD: extend `AutoCrud<T>` (T a record implementing `Identifiable`) and override the one mandatory method, `store()`, returning a `CrudStore<T>` (findById, save, findAll, deleteAllById).
- Custom listings: implement `Listing<Row>` (+ `Searchable`/`Filterable<F>` capabilities) and its `search(SearchRequest, HttpRequest)`.
- Wizard: extend `Wizard`, declare `WizardStep` fields, annotate the final action with `@WizardCompletionAction`.
- Dense screens: combine `@Compact` + `@Zones`/`@Zone` + `@Section(zone="...")`.
- Dynamic banners: `@Banner` on a method or implement `BannerSupplier`.
- Header badges: `@BadgeInHeader` on a field or implement `HeaderBadgesSupplier`.
- Floating buttons: `@Fab(icon="vaadin:plus")` on a method (app-level = global, page-level = scoped).
- Dark/light mode toggle: `@App(themeToggle=true)`.
- Unsaved-changes guard: `@ConfirmOnNavigationIfDirty` warns before leaving a modified form (menu, browser back/forward, reload/close); use `UICommand.markAsClean()` / `markAsDirty()` to control the state.
- Money formatting: `@Stereotype(FieldStereotype.money)` formats a numeric read-only/plain-text field as an amount in the UI's locale.
- Expression labels: any label supports `${state.field}` template expressions.
- URL pagination: CRUD pages sync `?page=N&sort=field:asc` to the URL automatically.
